pages.name: Seven quarters
pages.text: You've met 7/4 already. Seven quarters fill one whole bar and three quarters of the next. Written as 1 3/4, the same amount is called a [[mixed number]].

pages.alt: Two bars of 4 quarters, one above the other, and 7/4 written under them. 7 quarters are shaded and counted, filling the first bar, one whole, and 3 of the second. Beside the bars, 1 and 3/4; under them, 7/4 = 1 and 3/4.

pages.name: Colour one and a quarter
pages.why: 1 1/4 is one whole and one quarter more. The whole is the full bar of four quarters, and one more makes five, so 1 1/4 = 5/4.

pages.name: Sort into wholes
pages.text: Count how many wholes fit in 11/4, four quarters to each bar. Two fit, and the 3 left over stay quarters. So 11/4 = 2 3/4.

pages.alt: Three bars of 4 quarters, one above another, and 11/4 written under them. 11 of the 11 quarters are shaded and counted, four to a bar. Two bars are full, each labelled 1, and the third has 3 quarters, so 11/4 = 2 and 3/4.

pages.name: Nine quarters
pages.task: 9/4 has a top bigger than its bottom, so it is an [[improper fraction]]. Write it as a mixed number.
pages.why: Two bars hold eight of the quarters, so 2 wholes fit. The one left over stays a quarter, so 9/4 = 2 1/4.

pages.name: Seven thirds
pages.task: Colour 7 thirds, then write 7/3 as a mixed number.
pages.why: A whole is three thirds, so two wholes take six of the seven. The one left over is a third, so 7/3 = 2 1/3.

pages.name: Back the other way
pages.text: Now go the other way. Cut the whole into its 4 quarters and keep counting through the 3 more. The top is 1 × 4 + 3 = 7, over the same bottom, so 1 3/4 = 7/4.

pages.name: Two and a half in halves
pages.why: Each whole is 2 halves, so 2 wholes are 4 halves. One more half makes 5, so 2 1/2 = 5/2.

pages.name: A hole saw in eighths
pages.task: A hole saw is marked 1 3/8 inch. Write that in eighths of an inch.
pages.why: One inch is 8 eighths, and 3 more make 11. So 1 3/8 inch = 11/8 inch.

pages.name: One place on the line
pages.text: On the number line, 1 3/4 sits three quarter-steps past 1. Count quarter-steps from 0 instead, and the seventh lands in the same place. So 1 3/4 and 7/4 are the same number.

pages.name: Find 2 1/4 on the line
pages.why: Go 2 wholes from 0, then one quarter-step more. That is nine quarter-steps from 0, so 2 1/4 = 9/4.

pages.name: Seven half metres
pages.task: Seven lengths of cable are each 1/2 m long. How long are they end to end, in metres?
pages.why: Two halves make a metre, so seven halves fill 3 metres with one half left. That is 3 1/2 m.

pages.name: Not the same
pages.task: Which of these is not the same as 1 3/4?
pages.why: 7/4 is seven quarters, and 6/8 is the same as 3/4, so both match. 13/4 is thirteen quarters, which is 3 1/4.
